chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is permissible for the sick person to recite in the obligatory prayer only the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha), and it is permissible for the healthy person regarding the make-up of the voluntary prayer at night and during the day.

key_terms.بِاللَّيْلِ وَ النَّهَارِ: at night and during the day
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: the Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for recitation in prayer for a sick person and making up voluntary prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in recitation (qira'ah) based on physical capability and prayer type, reflecting the Shia principle of ease (taysir) in worship. It specifically permits a sick individual to recite only Surah Al-Fatiha in obligatory prayers, while allowing a healthy person to make up voluntary prayers (nawafil) at any time, highlighting the distinction between the strict requirements of fard and the leniency of sunnah. This ruling underscores the jurisprudential nuance that while Al-Fatiha is the pillar of recitation, additional surahs are not strictly mandatory for validity under all conditions.
